title: Does Eating Sour Candy Help with Anxiety? It Could Work as a Grounding Technique
titleZh: 为什么有人建议焦虑时，去尝尝酸味？
summary:
最近社交媒体上兴起一股风潮，建议人们在焦虑或惊恐发作时，通过含一颗酸味糖果来快速缓解情绪。但这种酸到让人皱眉的味道，真的对心理健康有什么帮助吗？这种做法背后的逻辑在于：只要酸味足够强烈，就能将人的注意力从引发焦虑的思绪中抽离出来——此时，你的注意力很可能会更多地集中在席卷味蕾的强烈酸味上。虽然酸味糖果绝非治疗焦虑的万能手段，但或许能作为一种短暂的注意力转移工具，让人暂时摆脱负面思绪。

来源：Discover；作者：Jack Knudson；原文发布时间：2026-05-12 20:03:00

paragraphs.contentEn: A recent social media trend has inspired people to pop a piece of sour candy into their mouth for a quick fix to anxiety and panic attacks. But does the mouth-puckering taste actually do anything for your mental health? The logic behind this trend is that a sour taste, if potent enough, can distract you from thoughts that cause anxiety — chances are, you'll start to focus more on the intense sourness overrunning your taste buds. While sour candy isn’t necessarily a cure-all for anxiety, it may work as a temporary distraction from negative thoughts.
paragraphs.contentZh: 最近社交媒体上兴起一股风潮，建议人们在焦虑或惊恐发作时，通过含一颗酸味糖果来快速缓解情绪。但这种酸到让人皱眉的味道，真的对心理健康有什么帮助吗？这种做法背后的逻辑在于：只要酸味足够强烈，就能将人的注意力从引发焦虑的思绪中抽离出来——此时，你的注意力很可能会更多地集中在席卷味蕾的强烈酸味上。虽然酸味糖果绝非治疗焦虑的万能手段，但或许能作为一种短暂的注意力转移工具，让人暂时摆脱负面思绪。

paragraphs.contentEn: When you consume something sour, whether it’s a piece of candy or a citrus fruit, chemical substances from the food or drink come into contact with taste receptor cells in the mouth. This interaction sends a message to the brain, specifically to a structure called the gustatory cortex, which processes taste. The gustatory cortex allows us to perceive the five basic tastes: salty, sour, bitter, sweet, and umami. It’s what makes us desire certain foods, like those high in natural sugars that fulfill important energy requirements, while also avoiding others that are unripe or spoiled, according to the University of Oregon.
paragraphs.contentZh: 无论是酸味糖果还是柑橘类水果，当人们摄入酸味食物时，食物或饮品中的化学物质都会与口腔内的味觉受体细胞结合。随后，这一刺激会向大脑传递信号，具体来说，是传递至负责处理味觉信息的味觉皮层。味觉皮层让人类能够感知五种基本味道：酸、甜、苦、咸和鲜。根据俄勒冈大学的说法，也正是这一系统，使人类会本能地偏好富含天然糖分、能够满足重要能量需求的食物，同时避开那些尚未成熟或已经变质的食物。

paragraphs.contentEn: So what does this mean for your mental health? If you're ever dwelling on thoughts that make you anxious, eating sour candy could work to your advantage as a grounding technique. This means that your brain will stay focused on the present, diverting your attention from distressing feelings. According to Utah State University Extension Professor Eva Timothy, the best way to approach this sour candy strategy is to pay attention to lingering flavors on your tongue, and the taste and smell. Rather than trying to cram down the candy right away, it’s more effective to keep that sour flavor in your mouth for as long as you can to concentrate on the taste.
paragraphs.contentZh: 那么，这对心理健康意味着什么？当你深陷焦虑思绪难以自拔时，一颗酸味糖果或许能作为一种接地技巧发挥作用。也就是说，它能让你的大脑保持对当下的专注，从而将注意力从困扰你的情绪上转移开。犹他州立大学推广教授伊娃·蒂莫西表示，运用酸糖策略的最佳方式是全神贯注于舌尖萦绕的味道，以及糖果的口感与气味。不要急着把糖果吃完，尽可能让酸味在口中停留更长时间，将注意力集中在这种味觉体验上，效果才会更加显著。

paragraphs.contentEn: There are plenty of other grounding techniques that make use of the five senses. The University of New Hampshire points to the “5-4-3-2-1” game as a strong example. The idea is to name five things you can see in your surroundings, four things you can feel, three things you can hear, two things you can smell, and one thing you can taste. By keeping yourself preoccupied with these tasks, anxiety-inducing thoughts may start to subside.
paragraphs.contentZh: 除了酸味糖果，其实还有许多利用五感的接地技巧。新罕布什尔大学推荐的“5-4-3-2-1”练习就是其中一个典型例子。这一方法的具体做法是，依次说出你周围能看到的5样东西、能感受到的4样东西、能听见的3种声音、能闻到的2种气味，以及能尝到的1种味道。当个体专注于完成这些任务时，那些引发焦虑的思绪可能会随之淡化。

paragraphs.contentEn: Certain sour foods can also impact your brain in other ways. Sour foods were found to promote risk-taking in a 2018 Scientific Reports study, for instance. In this study, researchers had participants ingest one of the five basic tastes before performing a Balloon Analogue Risk Test (BART), in which they would try to inflate a virtual balloon as much as they could, achieving a higher reward as the balloon got larger. However, if the balloon were pumped too much, it would potentially explode, getting rid of the reward.
paragraphs.contentZh: 此外，某些酸味食物还可能从其他层面影响大脑。例如，2018年发表在《科学报告》的一项研究发现，酸味食物可能会增强人的冒险倾向。在这项研究中，研究人员先让参与者摄入五种基本味道中的一种，随后再进行“气球模拟风险测试”（BART），在测试过程中，参与者需要尽可能给一个虚拟气球充气，气球越大，获得的奖励也越高。但如果充气过度，气球就可能爆炸，奖励也会随之归零。

paragraphs.contentEn: Participants who ingested sour foods ended up clicking more than others to inflate the balloon, showing that they were more likely to take on a greater risk of popping the balloon to maximize their potential reward. Based on these results, the researchers learned that there might be implications for risk-averse people (like people with anxiety or depression) to add sour foods to their diet. They noted that the risks taken don’t have to be as extreme as jumping out of a plane, for example. Rather, hypothetically, sour taste could encourage simple, everyday self-improvement behaviors like deciding to talk to a stranger or leave the house.
paragraphs.contentZh: 结果显示，相比于其他人，摄入酸味食物的参与者为气球充气的点击次数更多，这表明他们更愿意承担更大的气球爆炸风险，以最大化可能获得的奖励。基于这一结果，研究人员认为，对于那些本身更倾向于规避风险的人（例如焦虑或抑郁人群）来说，在饮食中加入酸味食物或许具有一定意义。不过，他们也强调，这里所说的冒险并不一定是指跳伞之类的极端行为。相反，从理论上来说，酸味刺激或许能够推动人们做出一些简单的、有助于自我突破的日常举动，比如主动和陌生人交流，或是愿意走出家门。
